question.body:
A particle has position $(x(t),y(t))$. At $t=1$, its position is $(2,6)$, and for $t>0$ its velocity vector is $(1-1/t^2, 2+1/t^2)$.

(a) Find the acceleration vector at $t=3$.

(b) Find the position at $t=3$.

(c) When does the tangent line to the path have slope $8$?

(d) The particle approaches a line as $t -> infinity$. Find the slope of this line and justify.
question.solution:
(a) The acceleration vector is $(2/t^3,-2/t^3)$, so at $t=3$ it is $(2/27,-2/27)$.

(b) Integrating gives $x=t+1/t+C_1$ and $y=2t-1/t+C_2$. The initial position gives $C_1=0$ and $C_2=5$, so the position at $t=3$ is $(10/3,32/3)$.

(c) $dif y/dif x=(2+1/t^2)/(1-1/t^2)=8$. Hence $t^2=3/2$, so $t=sqrt(3/2)$.

(d) $lim_(t -> infinity) dif y/dif x=lim_(t -> infinity) (2+1/t^2)/(1-1/t^2)=2$. The asymptotic line has slope $2$.
